transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, thank you so much for seeing me. Um, well, honestly, what made me come in today is... I guess it's a little embarrassing to admit, but I've been having some trouble at work. I'm in advertising sales, and we have these really long strategy meetings, and I just... I keep getting up when I know I’m supposed to stay seated. 

I try really hard not to be disruptive or anything! I usually just pretend I need to refill my water, or I'll go pace by the printer for a second just to stretch my legs. It's probably not the biggest deal in the world, but I know it doesn't look very professional, and I really want to do well at my job. Does that... does that make sense as a reason to come see you?
When you feel the urge to get up during those meetings, are you feeling anxious or worried about something?

Oh, no, definitely not anxious! I mean, I really like my job, and my team is great. It's not that I'm worried about the work or anything like that. It's more just... um, I don't know, my legs just decide they need to stretch? 

It's really just a little bit of pent-up energy, I guess. I'm totally fine mentally during the meetings! I just... get a little restless sitting in one chair for two hours straight. I feel like that's a pretty normal reaction to really long meetings, right? I'm not crazy for feeling that way, am I?
Besides feeling restless, do you also find it difficult to maintain your focus or attention during tasks at work?

Um... well, maybe just a little bit? I mean, I really try my best to pay attention, I promise I do! It's just... sometimes, like in those really long strategy meetings I mentioned, or, um, if I'm reading a really dense client brief... I'll start out super focused and ready to go. 

But then, after a few minutes, I'll suddenly realize I've just been staring at the exact same slide, or reading the same paragraph over and over, and I have absolutely no idea what the last point even was. I always catch myself and try to get right back on track, though! It's probably just because the briefs can get a little dry sometimes... I mean, that happens to everyone, right? It doesn't mean I'm doing a bad job, does it?

Um, distinct periods? Like, feeling really different for a few days? I don't... I don't think so. I mean, my mood is pretty steady, I'd say. I'm generally a pretty happy person! 

I definitely don't have, like, extreme highs or anything where I'm acting totally out of character. I mean, sure, if we land a big account, I'll be really excited for a couple of days, but that's just a normal reaction to good news, right? It's not like I'm doing anything crazy. I'm just... you know, happy about work! That's a good thing, isn't it? I really don't think I've ever had anything like what you're describing.

Um... well, maybe just a little? I really try my best to be a good listener, especially with my clients and my team! But... I guess sometimes, if I'm really excited about a pitch or a project, I might... sort of jump in with an answer before they've totally finished asking their question? 

It's really just because I'm so eager to help them out, you know? But then... yeah, sometimes I'll realize I completely answered the wrong thing because I didn't wait for the end of the sentence, or I just feel awful because I accidentally cut them off. I always apologize right away, though, and they usually laugh it off! It just means I'm really engaged and passionate about the work, right? I'm definitely not trying to be rude or talk over anyone, I promise!
Did you experience similar issues with restlessness or staying focused when you were a child, before the age of twelve?

Um... well, maybe? I mean, I was always a really happy kid, and I loved school! I think... I remember my mom keeping some of my old report cards from, like, elementary school, way before high school. 

My teachers always said I was really bright and enthusiastic, which is good, right? They did... um, they did sometimes write notes saying I rushed through things a bit, or that I would talk out of turn sometimes. And I guess I did forget my homework every now and then... oh, and my desk was usually a little messy, just stuffed with papers I hadn't quite finished yet. But I feel like a lot of kids are like that when they're little, aren't they? It's just normal kid energy, right? I was just really eager to learn and participate!

Both inattention (difficulty maintaining focus during long meetings and reading tasks, mind wandering) and hyperactivity/impulsivity (leaving seat during meetings, physical restlessness, blurting out answers and interrupting others) are present.
